meta.name: ILUD
meta.tagline: Use the internet with less AI.
meta.description: A researched catalogue of practical ways to turn off, work around, or replace unwanted AI features in the tools people use every day.
meta.maintenance: Every entry carries a confidence level, a verification date and its sources. Entries marked 'experimental' are community-discovered behaviour that platforms may change without notice. Re-check anything older than three months.
meta.disclaimer: ILUD is not affiliated with any of the services it describes. Nothing here asks you to break a rule, bypass payment, or install anything we have not named. Settings move. If a step no longer matches what you see, trust your screen over this page.

fixes.title: Make plain results your default
fixes.summary: Set your browser so every Google search skips the summary, without thinking about it again.
fixes.changes: Every search you type into the address bar goes straight to the plain list of links. Your browsing history, bookmarks and passwords are untouched.

action.label: Copy the search address
action.note: Paste this as a custom search engine in your browser settings. The %s is where your words go.

fixes.how: Browsers let you add your own search engine by giving it an address with a placeholder in it. Using Google's Web-filter address as that engine means the filter is applied before the page ever loads.
steps: Desktop Chrome or Edge: Settings → Search engine → Manage search engines → Add. Name it anything, shortcut anything, and paste the address above as the URL. Then set it as default.
Firefox: install the small "add custom search engine" add-on, or use a bookmark keyword with the address above.
Safari on iPhone: Safari cannot take a custom engine. Use the shortcut approach instead — add tenbluelinks.org to your Home Screen, or keep ILUD's search box handy.
Android Chrome: Settings → Search engine → Manage search engines → Add, same as desktop.
caveats: iOS Safari does not allow custom search engines. Third-party browsers on iPhone, such as Chrome or Firefox, do.
Some browser updates reset the default engine. Check it again after a major update.

sources.title: How to Disable Google AI Overviews: udm=14 & Alternatives

fixes.title: Search somewhere with no AI at all
fixes.summary: DuckDuckGo publishes an address that turns off every AI feature it has, permanently, for your browser.
fixes.changes: No generated answers, no assistant, no AI images in image search. Ordinary web results, and the same privacy behaviour DuckDuckGo is known for.
fixes.how: noai.duckduckgo.com is DuckDuckGo's own address for a version of the engine with every AI feature switched off. Visiting it stores that preference in your browser, so the ordinary address behaves the same way afterwards.
steps: Open noai.duckduckgo.com once in each browser you use.
The setting is stored in that browser. Clearing your site data resets it.
You can also set it feature by feature under Settings → AI Features on duckduckgo.com.
caveats: The preference lives in your browser's storage. Private windows and cleared cookies lose it.
DuckDuckGo's web results come partly from Bing's index, so what you find will differ from Google.

sources.title: How to filter out AI images in DuckDuckGo search results (official help)
Search engines that don't use AI (2026 survey)

fixes.title: Search without AI summaries
fixes.summary: Get the ordinary list of links back, with no generated answer on top.
fixes.changes: You see the classic list of web results. Nothing about your account changes, and you can go back to normal Google at any time by searching as usual.
fixes.how: Google's own "Web" filter — the tab that shows only website links — can be requested directly in the address of the page. ILUD adds that request for you, so the page opens already filtered. It is Google's own feature, not a trick against it.
steps: Search on Google as you normally would.
Under the search box, tap the Web tab. You may need to open the "More" menu to find it.
The generated summary disappears and only website links remain.
caveats: The Web view hides the Images, News, Maps and Videos shortcuts as well. Search again without the filter when you want them.
It applies to that one search. To make it permanent, set it as your default search engine — see the next entry.

alternatives.label: Use a search engine with no AI at all

sources.title: How to Turn Off Google AI Overviews and Get Traditional Search Results Back
How to Disable Google AI Overviews & Get Real Search Results (wikiHow)
Ten Blue Links — sets the Web filter as your default

fixes.title: Find small, hand-written websites
fixes.summary: A search engine that deliberately favours personal sites, essays and pages nobody optimised.
fixes.changes: You get the sort of page a person wrote because they cared about the subject. Almost nothing commercial surfaces.

action.label: Search the small web
action.placeholder: A subject you want to read about

fixes.how: Marginalia ranks pages roughly opposite to the usual way: it prefers plain documents, little advertising, and text that reads as though a human wrote it for another human.
caveats: Not useful for shopping, news, opening hours or anything time-sensitive.
Wonderful for hobbies, history, technical writing and rabbit holes.

fixes.title: Go straight to the encyclopedia
fixes.summary: For a fact, skip search entirely and read the article people wrote and argued over.
fixes.changes: You land on an encyclopedia article with visible authorship, citations and a full edit history.
fixes.how: Wikipedia's articles are written and reviewed by people, and every claim is supposed to carry a source you can follow. Generated summaries on the site remain experimental rather than the default for readers.
caveats: Wikipedia has its own biases and gaps. The citations at the foot of an article are the real prize.
Community debate about machine-assisted editing continues; reader-facing article text is still human-written.

fixes.title: Google's results, without Google's summary
fixes.summary: Startpage fetches Google's results for you and hands them over as plain links.
fixes.changes: The same results you would get from Google, with the summary, the assistant and the tracking stripped out along the way.
fixes.how: Startpage acts as a go-between. It runs your search against Google's index on its own servers and returns only the list of links, so the generated layer never reaches you.
caveats: Results can be a little slower than searching Google directly.
Google's own panels — Maps, Flights, Scholar — are not carried across.

sources.title: Best alternative search engines to Google in 2026

fixes.title: Hide AI-written websites from your results
fixes.summary: Subscribe to a maintained list of sites known for machine-written filler and they stop appearing in search.
fixes.changes: Results from listed domains are removed across Google, Bing, DuckDuckGo, Brave, Startpage and others.
fixes.how: uBlacklist is a browser add-on that removes chosen domains from search result pages. The community blocklist is a long, manually curated register of sites publishing generated text and images. Subscribing means the list keeps itself up to date.
steps: Install the uBlacklist add-on for Chrome, Edge or Firefox.
Open its options and choose "Add a subscription".
Paste the list address from the project page above.
Optionally add the stricter "nuclear" list, which also removes mixed sites that host both human and generated work.
caveats: The list is made by volunteers and will occasionally be wrong in both directions.
The stricter list removes large, legitimate sites such as stock libraries. Start with the ordinary list.
Firefox for Android supports add-ons. Safari and Chrome on iPhone do not.

fixes.title: Remove the summary automatically
fixes.summary: A small browser add-on strips the generated answer out of every Google page.
fixes.changes: Google looks almost exactly as it always did, minus the summary block. Other Google features keep working.
fixes.how: These add-ons either hide the summary element on the page, or quietly redirect your search to Google's own Web filter. Both leave the rest of the page intact.
steps: Open your browser's add-on store.
Look for "Hide Google AI Overviews", "Bye Bye Google AI" or "10 Blue Links". All three are widely used and do slightly different jobs.
Install one. There is nothing to configure afterwards.
caveats: Browser add-ons can read the pages you visit. Install ones with a visible author, a public source repository and a large number of users.
Mobile Safari and mobile Chrome do not support these. Firefox for Android does.

sources.title: Browser Extensions to Block Google AI Overview (2026)
Google AI Overview Disabler — Chrome Web Store

fixes.title: Pay for a search engine that obeys you
fixes.summary: A subscription search engine with no advertising, generated answers off by default, and the power to demote sites you dislike.
fixes.changes: You pay a monthly fee instead of being the product. You can permanently push chosen domains down, or off your results entirely.
fixes.how: Because there is no advertising to protect, Kagi lets you rank the web yourself: block a domain and it never appears again. Its summariser exists but stays off unless you ask for it.
caveats: It costs money. That is the trade, and it is a fair one to state plainly.
There is a free trial with a limited number of searches, so you can judge before paying.

fixes.title: Search an index nobody else owns
fixes.summary: An independent British search engine that crawls the web itself and shows only links.
fixes.changes: Different results from Google or Bing, because the index is genuinely separate. No summaries, no chat, no account.
fixes.how: Mojeek runs its own crawler and its own index. Very few engines in the world do, which is why its results feel different rather than merely re-skinned.
caveats: A smaller index means fewer results for obscure or very recent queries. Best as a second opinion rather than a sole engine.

sources.title: Search engines that don't use AI

fixes.title: Search only pages written before the flood
fixes.summary: Limit results to pages published before generated articles became common.
fixes.changes: You see older pages only. Excellent for reference, recipes and how-to writing; useless for anything current.

action.label: Search older pages
action.placeholder: A recipe, a how-to, a definition

fixes.how: Google supports a before: operator that limits results by publication date. Combined with the Web filter it gives you a list of older, human-written pages.
caveats: Publication dates on the web are frequently wrong, so the cut is approximate.
Unsuitable for news, prices, opening hours or anything that changes.

sources.title: How to filter AI images and content from Google search results

fixes.title: Turn off Brave's answer box
fixes.summary: Brave Search has a proper switch for its generated answers. Set it once.
fixes.changes: Brave Search returns to a plain list of results. Brave's browser assistant is a separate setting.
steps: Open search.brave.com and tap the settings icon.
Find the AI or Answers section.
Switch the answer box off. The preference is stored in your browser.
caveats: The setting is per-browser rather than per-account unless you are signed in.

sources.title: Best private search engines 2026, ranked and compared

fixes.title: Browse the old, hand-made web
fixes.summary: A small curated index of simple, personal pages of the kind the web used to be made of.
fixes.changes: Results are pages people built by hand. There is also a button that simply takes you somewhere at random.
fixes.how: Wiby's index is submitted and reviewed by people rather than crawled at scale, so everything in it was chosen by someone.
caveats: Tiny index. Treat it as a place to wander, not a reference tool.

sources.title: Wiby — search engine for the classic web

fixes.title: The blunt one: scare the summary away
fixes.summary: Adding one excluded word to a query often stops the summary appearing. It is crude, and it is not dependable.
fixes.changes: Your results are the usual ones. One word is excluded from them, which occasionally changes what you find.
fixes.how: Google's generated summaries are tied more tightly to its safety filters than its ordinary results are. A query containing a coarse term — even one you have explicitly excluded with a minus sign — can trip those filters, and the summary is simply not produced. The word ILUD appends is Russian profanity; it is there because it reliably trips the filter in English-language searches, not because it means anything useful. Nothing is sent anywhere but Google, and nothing is installed.
steps: Type your search as normal.
Add a space, then a minus sign, then a coarse word — any will do.
Search. The summary is often absent.
caveats: This is a side effect of a filter, not a feature. Google adjusts these filters regularly and the behaviour has come and gone before.
Excluding a word genuinely removes pages containing it, which can quietly change your results.
The Web filter does the same job properly. Use this only when something stops you using that.
Think twice on a shared or work computer where your search history is visible to others.

alternatives.label: The reliable way to do this

fixes.title: Get Meta AI out of the way on Instagram and Facebook
fixes.summary: There is no off switch. There is, however, a reliable way to make it stop appearing.
fixes.changes: The Meta AI conversation is muted and archived, so it stops surfacing in your inbox and notifications.
steps: Open your direct messages.
Swipe or long-press the Meta AI conversation.
Choose Mute, then Archive or Delete. Deleting removes it from your list until you interact again.
In the search bar, ignore the AI suggestion row; it cannot currently be removed.
Turn off AI-related notifications: Settings → Notifications, and switch off anything mentioning Meta AI.
fixes.how: Meta treats its assistant as a contact rather than a feature, which is why there is no switch — but it also means the ordinary tools for unwanted contacts work on it.
caveats: The AI search suggestion inside the app cannot be hidden.
In the EU and UK you have a separate right to object to your public posts being used for training — see the next entry.

sources.title: How to turn off Meta AI

fixes.title: Hide the Meta AI button in WhatsApp
fixes.summary: A setting now exists to remove the blue circle from your chat list.
fixes.changes: The floating Meta AI button disappears and the AI chat leaves your list. Your messages and groups are untouched.
steps: Open WhatsApp and go to Settings.
Tap Chats.
Find "Show Meta AI Button" and switch it off.
If you do not see it, update WhatsApp — the setting is being rolled out gradually and arrives at different times in different countries.
fixes.how: Meta added the toggle after sustained complaints. It hides the entry point rather than removing the service from WhatsApp's servers.
caveats: Not everyone has the setting yet. If it is missing, you can still archive the Meta AI chat so it stays out of the way.
Meta AI can still be summoned inside a chat by typing @Meta AI. Simply don't.
Your ordinary messages remain end-to-end encrypted; only what you actively send to Meta AI goes to Meta.

alternatives.label: Move to a messenger with no assistant

sources.title: How to turn off Meta AI on WhatsApp, Instagram and Facebook

fixes.title: Message on a platform with no assistant
fixes.summary: A messenger run by a non-profit, with no advertising, no AI features and no business model that needs them.
fixes.changes: Your conversations are end-to-end encrypted and there is no assistant in the app at all.
fixes.how: Signal is funded by donations through a non-profit foundation. It has no advertising business, and therefore no reason to build an assistant into your conversations.
caveats: Your correspondents have to be there too — that is the only real obstacle.
Requires a phone number to register, though usernames now hide it from contacts.

fixes.title: Object to your posts training Meta's AI
fixes.summary: In the UK and EU you can formally object, and Meta must honour it.
fixes.changes: Your public posts, photos and captions are excluded from Meta's generative AI training.
steps: Open Settings → Privacy Centre in the Facebook or Instagram app.
Find the notice about using your information for AI, or search Help for "object AI training".
Open the objection form and submit it. You do not have to give a reason in the EU or UK.
Repeat for each account. Facebook and Instagram are objected to separately unless they share an accounts centre.
fixes.how: European data protection law gives you a right to object to processing based on legitimate interest. Meta relies on that basis for training, so the objection has teeth.
caveats: Outside the EU, UK and a handful of other jurisdictions there is no equivalent right and no form.
Objecting does not remove data already used in models that have been trained.
Content other people have posted about you is not covered.

fixes.title: Put Facebook back in date order
fixes.summary: The chronological feed still exists, and you can bookmark it.
fixes.changes: Posts from friends and pages you follow, newest first, with no suggested content.
steps: On the website, the link above opens the most-recent view directly. Bookmark it.
In the app: tap the menu, then Feeds, then Friends or Favourites.
Add your favourite pages and people to Favourites so that feed is worth reading.
caveats: Facebook does not let you make this the default; you must go back to it each session.
The address form has changed before and may change again.

fixes.title: Read Reddit without the answer box
fixes.summary: Reddit Answers cannot be switched off, but a small add-on removes its links, and a plainer interface still exists.
fixes.changes: The generated answer prompts disappear from search and comment pages. Discussion threads read as they always did.
fixes.how: The add-on removes the Answers entry points from the page in your browser. It changes nothing on Reddit's side and sends nothing anywhere.
caveats: Reddit provides no setting to disable Answers.
old.reddit.com now requires you to be signed in and Reddit has said it is winding the old interface down, so do not rely on it.
Searching Reddit through Google with the Web filter is the most durable workaround and needs nothing installed.

fixes.title: Stop LinkedIn training on your profile
fixes.summary: A direct link to the one switch that matters.
fixes.changes: Your profile, posts and activity stop being used to improve LinkedIn's generative AI models.
fixes.how: LinkedIn turned this on by default for most members. The switch is buried several levels deep in settings, so ILUD links straight to it.
caveats: It is not retroactive: data already used in trained models stays there.
LinkedIn's writing suggestions and profile rewrites are separate features you simply need not use.

sources.title: LinkedIn — Data for generative AI improvement

fixes.title: Stop X from feeding your posts to Grok
fixes.summary: One checkbox stops your posts and interactions being used to train Grok.
fixes.changes: Your posts stop being used for training. Grok remains in the app but stops learning from you.
steps: Open Settings → Privacy and safety.
Tap "Grok & third-party collaborators".
Uncheck "Allow your public posts as well as your interactions, inputs and results with Grok to be used for training and fine-tuning".
While you are there, use "Delete conversation history" to clear anything you have already sent to Grok.
fixes.how: X exposes this as a genuine account setting rather than a regional concession, so it works wherever you are.
caveats: It is easier to find on the website than in the mobile app.
It does not remove Grok's summaries from trending topics or the explore tab.
Setting your account to protected also removes your posts from training.

fixes.title: A feed in the order things happened
fixes.summary: Social networks where the timeline is chronological by design and nothing recommends anything.
fixes.changes: You see posts from people you follow, newest first. No ranking, no suggested accounts, no generated filler.
fixes.how: These networks are run by many independent servers rather than one company. Without an advertising market there is no incentive to reorder your timeline.
caveats: Choosing a server is an unfamiliar first step; any of the large general ones is fine and you can move later.
Smaller audiences. Good for conversation, less good for reaching strangers.

fixes.title: Clear My AI from your Snapchat feed
fixes.summary: It cannot be deleted, but it can be unpinned and cleared out of the way.
fixes.changes: My AI stops sitting at the top of your chat list.
steps: Open the Chat screen.
Press and hold the My AI conversation.
Tap Chat Settings, then "Clear from Chat Feed".
Snapchat+ subscribers can also unpin it permanently.
caveats: It returns if you interact with it again.
Free accounts cannot remove it altogether; that is Snapchat's design, not an oversight on our part.

fixes.title: Know when a post was generated
fixes.summary: Every major platform now labels synthetic media. Learn where the label lives.
fixes.changes: You start noticing the small "AI info" or "AI-generated" marks that were always there.
steps: Instagram and Facebook: an "AI info" tag beneath the account name, or in the three-dot menu.
TikTok: an "AI-generated" sticker in the lower-left corner of the video.
YouTube: "Altered or synthetic content" in the expanded description.
If a post has no label but feels wrong, reverse-search a still from it.
fixes.how: Labels come from two sources: the uploader declaring it, and embedded provenance data written by the generating tool. Both are easy to strip, which is why the labels are a hint rather than a guarantee.
caveats: Absence of a label means nothing. Presence of one is reliable.
Re-uploads and screen recordings lose the embedded data.

sources.title: How to turn off Meta AI

fixes.title: Reset a feed that has learned the wrong things
fixes.summary: Start the recommendation engine from scratch, or turn personalisation off entirely.
fixes.changes: Your For You feed forgets what it thought it knew and begins again from your new behaviour.
steps: Profile → menu → Settings and privacy.
Content preferences → Refresh your For You feed.
For a harder stop: Settings → Ads → Personalisation and data, and switch personalisation off.
On individual videos, long-press → Not interested.
caveats: Turning personalisation off makes the app considerably less useful; many people prefer the reset.
Menu names move between app versions.

fixes.title: Hide AI images in image search
fixes.summary: DuckDuckGo has a real switch that filters generated pictures out of image results.
fixes.changes: Image results show far fewer generated pictures. It is a filter, not a guarantee — some slip through.

action.label: Search images without AI
action.placeholder: A photograph you are looking for

fixes.how: DuckDuckGo uses open, community-maintained blocklists of domains that mostly host generated imagery, and removes results from them. Opening the noai address switches every AI feature off at once, including this filter.
steps: Search for images on DuckDuckGo.
Open the dropdown above the results marked "AI images".
Choose "Hide". The choice is remembered in that browser.
caveats: The filter works on where an image is hosted, not on the image itself, so it cannot catch everything.
The preference is stored in your browser and is lost if you clear site data.

sources.title: How to filter out AI images in DuckDuckGo search results (official)

fixes.title: Check whether a picture is real
fixes.summary: Before you believe or share an image, find out where else it has appeared.
fixes.changes: You see the earliest and most credible places the image has been published, which usually settles the question.
fixes.how: A generated image has no history. A real photograph almost always does — a news agency, a photographer's portfolio, an older post. TinEye sorts by oldest first, which is exactly what you want.
steps: Save or copy the image.
Upload it to TinEye and sort results by "Oldest".
No history at all, or a first appearance on a content farm, is a strong signal.
caveats: Automatic AI-detection tools are unreliable in both directions. Provenance is better evidence than a detector's score.
Cropped or re-compressed images are harder to trace.

fixes.title: Fewer generated pictures on Google Images
fixes.summary: Google has no filter, so exclude the words that generated images are usually tagged with.
fixes.changes: Results lose pages that mention the common generator names. It thins the flood; it does not stop it.

action.label: Search images, minus the obvious
action.placeholder: A photograph you are looking for

fixes.how: udm=2 is Google's own Images view. The minus terms remove pages whose text names the usual generators, which is how a great deal of generated imagery is labelled by the sites that host it.
caveats: Only as good as the labelling. Unlabelled generated images sail straight through.
It will also remove legitimate pages that happen to discuss AI.
Adding before:2023 to the query is a blunter but often more effective filter.

sources.title: How to filter AI images and content from Google search results

fixes.title: Free photographs taken by photographers
fixes.summary: Large libraries of real photographs with clear licensing and a named person behind each one.
fixes.changes: Every result has an author, a camera and a licence. You can use them, with attribution, without wondering where they came from.
fixes.how: These libraries index openly-licensed work from museums, archives, government agencies and individual photographers. Provenance is part of the record rather than an afterthought.
caveats: Generated images do appear in large user-upload libraries. Check the author's other work if it matters.
Flickr asks uploaders to tag AI-generated work; enforcement is imperfect.

fixes.title: Look at art made by people
fixes.summary: A portfolio community for artists that does not permit generated work.
fixes.changes: Everything you see is presented as human-made, and the rule is enforced by the platform and its members.
fixes.how: Cara was founded in direct response to generated work flooding portfolio sites. Generated images are against its rules and it applies detection alongside human moderation.
caveats: Best for illustration, concept art and design rather than documentary photography.
Smaller than the big platforms, which is rather the point.

fixes.title: Show photographs only
fixes.summary: Bing can restrict image results to photographs, which removes most generated art in one step.
fixes.changes: Illustrations, clip art, line drawings and most generated imagery disappear. Only photographs remain.
fixes.how: Bing classifies images by type. Asking for the photograph type excludes the illustration and drawing categories where most generated work is filed.
steps: Search Bing Images.
Open Filter → Type → Photograph.
caveats: Photorealistic generated images are still classed as photographs and will appear.
Bing also offers a Licence filter, which pairs well with this.

sources.title: How to filter AI images from search results

fixes.title: Blur out AI images everywhere
fixes.summary: An add-on that detects and hides generated images across search engines and social sites.
fixes.changes: Suspected generated images are hidden or blurred as pages load, on Google, Bing, DuckDuckGo, Pinterest and others.
fixes.how: The add-on combines domain blocklists with image analysis, so it catches some images that a domain list alone would miss.
caveats: Detection of generated imagery is imperfect by nature. Expect both misses and false alarms.
Desktop browsers only.
It inspects images on pages you visit; read its privacy statement before installing.

fixes.title: See fewer generated pins
fixes.summary: Pinterest added controls to reduce generated imagery in the categories where it bothers people most.
fixes.changes: Your home feed shows fewer generated pins in the categories you adjust. Labels appear on pins Pinterest believes were generated.
steps: Open Pinterest settings while signed in.
Look under Privacy and data, or the "Refine your recommendations" controls.
Reduce generated content for the categories offered — beauty, art, fashion and home decor were the first supported.
On individual pins, use the three-dot menu → "See less like this".
caveats: The control is applied per category rather than everywhere, and coverage varies by region.
It reduces rather than removes.

fixes.title: Stock photography without the generated shelf
fixes.summary: The big free-photo sites now carry generated work. Here is how to see past it.
fixes.changes: You still get high-quality photographs, with the generated material filtered or avoided.

alternatives.label: Public domain archives at Flickr Commons

fixes.how: Most large libraries now require uploaders to label generated content, and many surface a filter. The labels are the thing to look for on the image page before you use it.
caveats: Labelling is self-declared and inconsistent.
If provenance genuinely matters — journalism, history, evidence — use an archive or a named photographer's own site instead.

fixes.title: Commission a person instead
fixes.summary: If you need an image made, hiring an illustrator is often quicker and cheaper than people assume.
fixes.changes: You get something made for your purpose, with rights you can actually rely on, by someone who will answer your questions.
fixes.how: Portfolio sites are searchable by style and medium, and most artists publish their commission terms and rates openly.
caveats: Behance and ArtStation both host generated work; both now label it and allow you to filter. Check the artist's process posts.
Agree licence and usage in writing before work begins.

fixes.title: Remove Gemini from Gmail and Docs
fixes.summary: One pair of switches turns off the generative features across Gmail, Docs, Sheets and Drive.
fixes.changes: The Gemini side panel, "Help me write", smart replies and inbox summaries all disappear. Your documents and mail are untouched.
steps: Open Gmail on the web and go to Settings → See all settings → General.
Find "Google Workspace smart features".
Click "Manage Workspace smart feature settings".
Switch off both toggles: smart features in Workspace, and smart features in other Google products.
Save. Reload Gmail and Docs; the Gemini buttons are gone.
fixes.how: Google gates its generative features in Workspace behind the same consent flag as its older "smart" features. Withdrawing that consent removes the whole layer rather than hiding individual buttons.
caveats: It also disables Smart Compose, smart reply, automatic inbox categories and package tracking. Some people miss these; the switch is easy to reverse.
On a work or school account, an administrator may have locked the setting.
Grammar and spelling checks in Docs are part of the same bundle.

sources.title: Turn smart features and personalisation on or off (official)

fixes.title: Turn off Copilot in Word, Excel and Outlook
fixes.summary: Each desktop app has a proper checkbox. Untick it and the button goes away.
fixes.changes: The Copilot ribbon button and the margin prompt disappear from that app on that computer.
steps: Open Word. Go to File → Options.
Choose Copilot in the left-hand list.
Untick "Enable Copilot".
Restart Word. Repeat in Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook and OneNote — the setting is per application.
fixes.how: Microsoft added a per-application switch after complaints about the button appearing unbidden. It is stored per device and per app.
caveats: Only available on personal Microsoft accounts. Work and school accounts are controlled by an administrator.
Per computer: repeat on each machine you use.
The web versions of Office have their own, separate controls.

sources.title: Turn Microsoft 365 Copilot on or off (official)

fixes.title: Get the Gemini button out of Google Docs
fixes.summary: If you want to keep smart features, you can still remove the writing assistant from the page.
fixes.changes: The "Help me write" pill and the Gemini icon leave the document. Everything else stays.
steps: Open any document.
Click the Gemini icon in the top-right, then the settings or three-dot menu inside the panel.
Choose "Bottom bar preferences" and untick "Write with Gemini".
Collapse the side panel with the arrow at its edge.
caveats: It hides the entry points rather than disabling the service. The full switch is the Workspace smart features one above.
Google moves this menu regularly.

alternatives.label: Turn the whole thing off instead

fixes.title: Remove Writing Tools from the text menu
fixes.summary: Stop "Rewrite", "Proofread" and "Summarise" appearing whenever you select text.
fixes.changes: The text selection menu returns to Cut, Copy, Paste and Look Up.
steps: iPhone or iPad: Settings → Apple Intelligence & Siri → turn Apple Intelligence off, or turn off Writing Tools specifically.
Mac: System Settings → Apple Intelligence & Siri → same controls.
For a permanent block a child or colleague cannot undo: Settings → Screen Time → Content & Privacy Restrictions → Intelligence & Siri.
caveats: Turning Apple Intelligence off entirely also removes notification summaries, Clean Up in Photos and the new Siri behaviour. Many people consider that a bonus.
It frees several gigabytes of storage, since the on-device models are deleted.

fixes.title: Stop your phone finishing your sentences
fixes.summary: Predictive text and generated suggestions are separate from autocorrect, and can go alone.
fixes.changes: The suggestion strip above the keyboard goes quiet. Autocorrect keeps fixing typos if you want it to.
steps: iPhone: Settings → General → Keyboard. Switch off Predictive. Leave Auto-Correction on if you like it.
iPhone with Apple Intelligence: also turn off Writing Tools under Settings → Apple Intelligence & Siri.
Android with Gboard: Settings → System → Languages & input → On-screen keyboard → Gboard → Text correction. Switch off "Show suggestion strip" and "Next-word suggestions".
Samsung Keyboard: Settings → General management → Samsung Keyboard settings → Predictive text off.
caveats: Autocorrect and prediction are different things. Turning off prediction leaves spelling correction intact.
Some keyboards reset these after major updates.

fixes.title: Write somewhere that offers nothing
fixes.summary: Editors built around a blank page, where nothing suggests, completes or rewrites.
fixes.changes: You open the app and there is text and a cursor. Files are plain text on your own disk.
fixes.how: These editors store Markdown files in ordinary folders. Obsidian is free for personal use and has no generative features unless you install a plugin; iA Writer marks any pasted text so you always know what you wrote.
caveats: iA Writer and Ulysses are paid. Obsidian is free for personal use.
No real-time collaboration in the Google Docs sense.

fixes.title: An email client with nothing in the margin
fixes.summary: Mail applications that do not offer to write your messages for you.
fixes.changes: A compose window with a cursor in it. Nothing suggests, summarises or replies on your behalf.
fixes.how: Thunderbird is free, open-source and run by a non-profit; it connects to your existing Gmail or Outlook account and shows you your mail without the web interface's additions.
caveats: Using a separate client does not stop Google or Microsoft processing the mail on their servers. For that you need the Workspace switch above, or a different provider.
Fastmail and Proton are paid services.

fixes.title: Keep the grammar check, lose the ghostwriter
fixes.summary: Grammarly separates its generative writing from its corrections. You can keep one.
fixes.changes: Suggestions to rewrite or generate whole passages stop appearing. Spelling and grammar corrections remain.
steps: Sign in at account.grammarly.com.
Open Account Settings → Customize or Personalization.
Switch off the generative AI assistance options.
caveats: Grammarly's core checking has always used machine learning; this switch concerns the generative features only.
On a business plan an administrator may control it.

fixes.title: Quieten Notion's assistant
fixes.summary: Stop the AI prompt appearing every time you press space on a new line.
fixes.changes: The "Ask AI" hint disappears from empty blocks. The rest of Notion is unchanged.
steps: Open Settings → Preferences (or Notion settings → My settings).
Find the AI section and switch off the inline AI trigger.
Workspace owners can disable Notion AI for the whole workspace under Settings → AI.
caveats: Member-level settings only hide the prompts; a workspace owner must disable the feature entirely.
Notion changes its settings layout frequently.

fixes.title: Turn off code completion suggestions
fixes.summary: A genuine, complete off switch — both in your account and in the editor.
fixes.changes: Suggestions stop appearing as you type. You can turn it off for one language, one file, or entirely.
steps: Visit github.com/settings/copilot to control the account-level subscription and data use.
In VS Code: click the Copilot status icon in the status bar → Disable Completions, globally or for the current language.
In JetBrains IDEs: the Copilot icon in the status bar has the same menu.
To remove it completely, uninstall the extension.
caveats: Organisation-provided Copilot seats may be controlled by your employer.
Turning off completions still leaves the chat panel; disable both if you want silence.

fixes.title: Skip the review summary, read the reviews
fixes.summary: Sort by most recent and filter to verified purchases to get past the generated digest.
fixes.changes: You read what people actually wrote, newest first, from confirmed buyers.
steps: On a product page, scroll to reviews and tap "See more reviews".
Change the sort from "Top reviews" to "Most recent".
Filter to "Verified purchase only".
Read the three-star reviews first; they are almost always the most informative.
fixes.how: The generated summary is built from the same reviews but flattens the disagreements, which are the part worth reading. Sorting by recency also catches products whose quality changed after a good early run.
caveats: Fake reviews exist regardless. Reviews mentioning specific, checkable details are the trustworthy ones.
Third-party checkers of review authenticity vary in quality; treat their scores as one signal.

fixes.title: Shop on Amazon without the assistant
fixes.summary: There is no setting. On a computer an add-on removes it; on the phone it can only be ignored.
fixes.changes: On desktop, the assistant panel and its prompts are hidden. On mobile, nothing changes and we will not pretend otherwise.
fixes.how: Amazon's shopping assistant — originally Rufus, now folded into the search bar as Alexa for Shopping — has no account setting at all. Community add-ons hide the panel using ordinary page-blocking rules.
steps: Search your browser's add-on store for "Adios Alexa for Shopping" or "Rufus Remover".
Install and reload Amazon.
On the phone, the only remedy is to use the mobile website in a browser with content blocking, or to ignore the prompt.
caveats: Amazon has moved and renamed this feature twice in two years; add-ons lag behind each change.
There is genuinely no way to turn it off in the Amazon mobile app.
Amazon's review summaries at the top of a listing are a separate generated feature, also not removable.

fixes.title: Show handmade things only
fixes.summary: Etsy can restrict results to items the seller has declared handmade.
fixes.changes: Resold factory goods and print-on-demand listings drop out of the results.

action.label: Search handmade only
action.placeholder: A gift, a piece of jewellery, a print

fixes.how: Etsy records whether a seller declared an item handmade. The filter is not always shown in the interface, but the site honours it when asked for directly.
caveats: It relies on the seller's declaration, which is not audited. Generated artwork printed onto a mug can still be listed as handmade.
Check the shop's process photographs and reviews. Real makers show their workshop.
Etsy has removed and reinstated this filter from its visible interface before.

fixes.title: Buy second-hand from a person
fixes.summary: Used listings are written by individuals, photographed by them, and nothing about them is generated.
fixes.changes: Blurred kitchen-table photographs and honest descriptions of wear. Cheaper, and far more informative.
fixes.how: The link filters eBay to used condition, where private sellers dominate and listings are made by hand.
caveats: Private sales have fewer protections than retail. Use the platform's payment system, never a direct bank transfer.
Some professional resellers now use generated descriptions; the photographs give them away.

fixes.title: Compare prices without a chatbot
fixes.summary: Tools that show price history and stock, and nothing else.
fixes.changes: You see a graph of what a thing has actually cost over time, which settles most "is this a deal" questions.
fixes.how: Price history sites track listings over months and years. A sale price that matches the median is not a sale.
caveats: Coverage is best for Amazon and patchier elsewhere.
Regional coverage varies considerably.

fixes.title: Find the maker's own website
fixes.summary: The simplest way past a marketplace's machinery is to buy directly from the person.
fixes.changes: No recommendation engine, no summary, no fees taken from the maker, and usually a real email address.
fixes.how: Search for the name with the large marketplaces excluded. Most small makers have their own shop with better prices and more information about how things are made.
caveats: Small shops have less generous returns policies. Check before buying.
Use a payment method with buyer protection when buying from an unfamiliar site.

fixes.title: Marketplaces that ban generated work
fixes.summary: Smaller shops whose rules require the maker and the item to be real.
fixes.changes: Everything is made by a person, and the person is usually reachable.
fixes.how: These platforms vet sellers individually rather than by self-declaration, and several explicitly prohibit AI-generated designs in their terms.
caveats: Smaller catalogues and sometimes slower shipping.
Big Cartel hosts independent shops rather than acting as a marketplace, so there is no unified search.

fixes.title: One panel for every AI feature in Firefox
fixes.summary: Firefox gathered all of its AI features into a single settings page you can switch off.
fixes.changes: The sidebar chatbot, link previews, tab-group suggestions and AI alt text all stop.

action.label: Copy the settings address
action.note: A web page is not allowed to open browser settings for you. Paste this into Firefox's address bar and scroll to AI Controls.

steps: Paste about:preferences#privacy into the address bar.
Scroll to "AI Controls".
Switch off everything you do not want. There is a master switch and per-feature ones.
Firefox 148 and later. If you do not see the panel, update.
fixes.how: Mozilla responded to complaints by consolidating what had been a dozen hidden preferences into one visible panel. It is the most honest arrangement any major browser currently offers.
caveats: Older Firefox versions need about:config instead — see the next entry.
Firefox for Android has a reduced version of the panel.

sources.title: Mozilla Support — AI features in Firefox

fixes.title: Quieten Safari and Apple Intelligence
fixes.summary: Turn off summaries, notification digests and the new Siri in one place.
fixes.changes: Page summaries, mail and message summaries and notification digests all stop. Several gigabytes of storage are returned.
steps: Settings → Apple Intelligence & Siri.
Turn Apple Intelligence off for everything, or use the per-feature switches below it.
Notification summaries are separate: Settings → Notifications → Summarise Notifications.
Mail summaries: Mail → Settings → Summarise previews.
To lock it so it cannot be turned back on: Settings → Screen Time → Content & Privacy Restrictions → Intelligence & Siri.
caveats: Turning it off deletes the downloaded models, which takes a few minutes and frees storage.
Siri still works; it reverts to its older behaviour.
Apple Intelligence is not available in every language or region anyway.

fixes.title: Remove Copilot from Windows
fixes.summary: Take the button off the taskbar, and stop the app starting with the system.
fixes.changes: The Copilot icon disappears and the assistant no longer opens on the keyboard shortcut.
steps: Settings → Personalisation → Taskbar → turn off Copilot.
Settings → Apps → Installed apps → find Copilot → Uninstall. It is an ordinary app and can be removed.
Settings → Apps → Startup → turn off anything Copilot-related.
To remap the Copilot key on newer keyboards: Settings → Personalisation → Text input → Customise Copilot key.
caveats: Windows updates sometimes reinstall the app. Check after a feature update.
Windows Pro and Enterprise can block it permanently by policy; Home cannot.

fixes.title: Turn off Chrome's AI features
fixes.summary: Recent Chrome versions have a dedicated AI settings page.
fixes.changes: Gemini in the browser, tab organiser, "help me write" and AI history search are switched off.

action.label: Copy the settings address
action.note: Chrome does not permit a web page to open its settings. Paste this into the address bar.

steps: Paste chrome://settings/ai into the address bar.
Switch off each feature listed.
If the page does not exist, update Chrome, or try chrome://settings/aiInnovations.
For features with no setting yet, chrome://flags lets you disable them — search for "AI" and set the relevant entries to Disabled.
caveats: Google adds AI features faster than it adds switches for them. Check this page after major updates.
chrome://flags is developer territory; changes there can be reset without warning.
On a managed work device, your employer's policy takes precedence.

fixes.title: Make sure Recall is not watching
fixes.summary: Check and switch off the feature that takes periodic snapshots of your screen.
fixes.changes: No more snapshots are saved, and existing ones can be deleted.
steps: Settings → Privacy & security → Recall & snapshots.
Turn off "Save snapshots".
Use "Delete snapshots" to remove everything already stored.
Add any application you never want captured to the exclusion list.
If the page is absent, your computer does not support Recall and there is nothing to do.
fixes.how: Recall only runs on Copilot+ hardware. It is opt-in after the 2025 redesign, but checking costs nothing and settles the question.
caveats: Snapshots are stored locally and encrypted, but anyone who can unlock your computer can read them.
Private browsing windows are excluded automatically; other applications are not.

fixes.title: Put the old assistant back on Android
fixes.summary: Stop Gemini or Galaxy AI taking over the button and the long-press.
fixes.changes: The assistant reverts to its older, narrower behaviour, or is removed from the gesture entirely.
steps: Settings → Apps → Default apps → Digital assistant app. Choose "None" to remove it from the gesture entirely.
In the Gemini app: profile picture → Settings → turn off Gemini in apps, and clear Gemini Apps Activity.
Samsung: Settings → Advanced features → Galaxy AI → turn off the features you do not want, and enable "Process data only on device".
Turn off the side-key or power-button assistant shortcut under Settings → Advanced features → Side button.
caveats: Menu paths differ by manufacturer and Android version more than on any other platform.
Some Google apps re-enable their own assistant entry points independently.

fixes.title: Remove Copilot from Edge
fixes.summary: Hide the sidebar button and stop the assistant appearing on pages.
fixes.changes: The Copilot icon leaves the toolbar and the sidebar. Edge behaves like an ordinary browser.

action.label: Copy the settings address
action.note: Paste this into Edge's address bar.

steps: Paste edge://settings/sidebar into the address bar.
Open the Copilot entry and turn off "Show Copilot".
Also check Settings → Appearance and turn off the Copilot toolbar button.
Under Settings → Privacy, turn off "Page context" so Copilot cannot read what you are viewing.
caveats: Microsoft has reinstated the button after some updates. Check again after a major Edge release.
Windows may still show Copilot in the taskbar; that is a separate setting.

fixes.title: Stop Google keeping your AI conversations
fixes.summary: Turn off Gemini Apps Activity and delete what is stored.
fixes.changes: Your conversations stop being saved to your account and stop being used for review or training.
steps: Open the link and turn off Gemini Apps Activity.
Delete the existing history from the same page.
While you are there, review Web & App Activity and YouTube History under myactivity.google.com.
caveats: Google states that conversations may still be retained for a period for safety review even when activity is off.
Turning it off removes your conversation history, which some people rely on.

fixes.title: Firefox, stripped back by hand
fixes.summary: For older versions, or for absolute certainty, set the preferences directly.
fixes.changes: Every AI subsystem in the browser is switched off at the preference level, including ones with no visible setting.

action.label: Copy the preference list
action.text:
browser.ml.enable = false
browser.ml.chat.enabled = false
browser.sidebarAI.enabled = false
browser.linkPreviews.enabled = false
browser.tabGroups.ai.enabled = false
browser.pdf.AIAltText.enabled = false
action.note: Open about:config, accept the warning, then search each name and set it to false.

steps: Type about:config in the address bar and accept the warning.
Search for each preference name in turn.
Double-click to set it to false. Create it as a Boolean if it does not exist.
Restart Firefox.
caveats: Preference names change between versions. If one does not exist, skip it.
about:config is unsupported territory; nothing here can harm your data, but make a note of what you changed.

sources.title: Mozilla Support — AI features in Firefox

fixes.title: Switch off Brave's Leo
fixes.summary: Brave lets you remove its assistant completely, which is more than most.
fixes.changes: The Leo icon disappears from the sidebar and the address bar suggestions.

action.label: Copy the settings address
action.note: Paste this into Brave's address bar.

steps: Paste brave://settings/leo-ai into the address bar.
Turn off "Show Leo icon in sidebar" and "Show Leo in the address bar".
On mobile: Settings → Brave Leo → Show in address bar, off.
caveats: Brave Search's answer box is a separate setting on search.brave.com.

fixes.title: Block AI services at the network level
fixes.summary: For a whole household: stop AI endpoints resolving at all.
fixes.changes: Chosen AI services simply fail to load on every device on the network.
fixes.how: The same community project that maintains the search blocklist publishes a hosts-file version. Feeding it to Pi-hole, AdGuard Home or NextDNS blocks those domains for everything on your network.
caveats: Blocking at DNS level breaks things in confusing ways; the failure looks like a network fault, not a block.
Some blocked domains are shared with non-AI services.
Requires a Pi-hole, a router that supports custom DNS, or a NextDNS account.

fixes.title: Turn off Opera's Aria
fixes.summary: Remove the assistant from the sidebar and the command line.
fixes.changes: Aria's icon disappears and the browser stops offering it.

action.label: Copy the settings address
action.note: Paste into Opera's address bar, then find the AI or Aria section.

steps: Open opera://settings.
Find Features or AI services and turn Aria off.
Right-click the sidebar to remove the icon as well.
caveats: Opera renames this section between releases.

fixes.title: Open YouTube on your subscriptions
fixes.summary: Bookmark the subscriptions page and never see the recommendation engine again.
fixes.changes: You see new videos from channels you chose, in date order. Nothing is suggested.
fixes.how: The subscriptions feed is a straightforward chronological list. It is the only part of YouTube that does exactly what you asked it to.
steps: Open the link above and bookmark it, or add it to your phone's home screen so it opens like an app.
On iPhone: Share → Add to Home Screen. On Android: menu → Add to Home screen.
caveats: The mobile app always opens on Home. The home-screen shortcut opens the website instead, which is the point.
Keeping your subscription list tidy matters more once this is your main view.

fixes.title: Stop YouTube recommending things
fixes.summary: Pause your watch history and the home page stops trying to guess what you want.
fixes.changes: The home page empties out and stops recommending. Subscriptions, search and playlists keep working exactly as before.
steps: Open the link and choose "Turn off" under YouTube History.
Optionally delete what is already there, or set automatic deletion after 3 months.
Return to YouTube. The home page is now blank, with a note explaining why.
fixes.how: YouTube's recommendations are built almost entirely from watch history. Remove the input and the output stops.
caveats: You lose "continue watching" and your viewing history list.
Some people find the empty home page liberating and others find it disorienting. It is reversible in one tap.

alternatives.label: Keep history but watch only subscriptions

fixes.title: Buy music from the people who made it
fixes.summary: A shop where musicians upload their own work, write their own notes and are paid directly.
fixes.changes: You buy a file you keep, from an artist who receives most of the money.
fixes.how: Bandcamp pages are made by the artists themselves. There is no recommendation engine pushing you anywhere, and the editorial writing is done by human critics.
caveats: Generated music does exist on Bandcamp; the artist page usually makes the difference obvious.
Not a streaming replacement — it is a shop and a discovery tool.

fixes.title: Filter AI-generated music out
fixes.summary: Deezer is the only major streaming service that lets you hide fully AI-generated tracks.
fixes.changes: Tracks Deezer identifies as fully machine-generated are labelled, excluded from editorial playlists and can be filtered from recommendations.
fixes.how: Deezer built a detector for the signatures left by the common music generators, and made the results visible to listeners rather than keeping them internal. Tagged tracks are excluded from editorial and algorithmic recommendation.
caveats: Detection catches fully generated tracks, not songs where a person used AI tools as part of their process.
Requires a Deezer account; a free tier exists.
Spotify labels some AI accounts but offers no listener-facing filter.

sources.title: Deezer AI music tagging and detection

fixes.title: Strip YouTube down to what you asked for
fixes.summary: An add-on that lets you remove the recommendation sidebar, the home feed, Shorts and comments.
fixes.changes: YouTube becomes a video player with a search box. You choose which parts return.
fixes.how: The add-on hides page elements in your browser. YouTube's servers are unaffected, so nothing about your account changes.
caveats: Desktop and Firefox for Android only.
YouTube redesigns break these add-ons from time to time; the popular ones are usually patched within days.

fixes.title: Teach YouTube to stop suggesting something
fixes.summary: "Not interested" and "Don't recommend channel" genuinely work, if you use them consistently.
fixes.changes: Specific videos and whole channels stop appearing in your recommendations.
steps: Tap the three dots on any recommended video.
Choose "Not interested", or better, "Don't recommend channel".
To undo past damage, open your history and remove individual videos that sent the algorithm astray.
fixes.how: These signals are weighted heavily. Channel-level blocking is far stronger than per-video dismissal, and persists.
caveats: It only affects the account you are signed into on that profile.
Watching even a few seconds of something is a stronger positive signal than "not interested" is a negative one.

sources.title: Manage your recommendations and search results (official)

fixes.title: Turn off the Shorts feed
fixes.summary: The endless vertical feed can be collapsed, hidden, or time-limited.
fixes.changes: Shorts stop appearing on the home page and the Shorts tab disappears or is limited.
steps: In the app: Settings → General → Manage all history, or Settings → Time management.
Look for the Shorts limit and set it, which hides the feed for the chosen period.
On the home page: tap the three dots on a Shorts shelf and choose "Not interested" — it hides that shelf for 30 days.
On desktop, the Unhook add-on removes Shorts and much else permanently.
caveats: YouTube keeps moving this setting and the 30-day hide expires.
The desktop add-on is the only permanent removal.

fixes.title: Let a human choose the music
fixes.summary: Stations where a person picks the records and tells you what they are.
fixes.changes: You hear a sequence someone thought about, with context, and you discover things no engine would have offered you.
fixes.how: Community and public stations run on human programming by constitution. Radio Garden lets you spin a globe and listen to any of them.
caveats: You cannot skip tracks. That is the arrangement, and much of the pleasure.

fixes.title: Stop the next thing starting by itself
fixes.summary: Turn off autoplay previews and next-episode autoplay, per profile.
fixes.changes: Nothing moves or plays until you ask it to. Browsing becomes quiet.
steps: Open your Netflix account page on the website — the setting does not exist in the mobile app.
Choose a profile, then Playback settings.
Uncheck both autoplay options. Repeat for each profile.
caveats: Per profile, not per account.
Other services bury the equivalent setting in different places; look under Playback or Accessibility.

fixes.title: Stop others remixing your videos with AI
fixes.summary: If you post to YouTube, you can prevent your Shorts being used as raw material for generated remixes.
fixes.changes: Your videos can no longer be fed into YouTube's generative remix tools by other users.
steps: Open YouTube Studio and go to the Shorts section of Content.
Edit a video, find "Shorts remixing".
Choose "Allow only audio remixing", or turn remixing off entirely.
Set it for existing videos as well as new uploads; it is per-video.
caveats: There is no single account-wide switch yet, which makes this tedious for large channels.
Rolled out gradually; not every account sees it.

fixes.title: Get a human on the line
fixes.summary: The words and buttons that most reliably escape an automated support agent.
fixes.changes: You are transferred to a person instead of looping through a menu or a chatbot.
steps: Say or type "agent", "representative", "operator" or "speak to a human". Repeat if it deflects.
On a phone menu, press 0 repeatedly. If that fails, press nothing at all — many systems transfer after two timeouts.
Say "complaint" or "cancel my account". Retention and complaints queues are almost always staffed by people.
In a chat window, type "human" three times in a row; many bots have an explicit escalation rule for this.
Failing all that, post publicly on the company's social media account. Those are monitored by people.
fixes.how: Most support systems have an escalation path, because regulators and refund costs require one. The trick is knowing the words that trigger it rather than the words the menu offers you.
caveats: Saying "cancel" may start an actual cancellation flow. Be ready to say you have changed your mind.
Some companies now have no human channel at all for free accounts. Written complaints and chargebacks are the remaining levers.

fixes.title: A recipe, without the life story or the generated blog
fixes.summary: Go straight to the ingredients and the method.
fixes.changes: You get a list and steps instead of nine hundred words and a chatbot.
fixes.how: Restricting the search to kitchens that test their recipes avoids the enormous quantity of generated recipe content now flooding search. Browser reader mode then strips the preamble.
steps: Search using the button above.
On the page, use your browser's Reader view — the icon in the address bar on iPhone and Firefox, or Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+R.
Most recipe sites also have a "Jump to recipe" link at the top.
caveats: Some of these sites are subscription-based.
A recipe with no photographs of the finished dish in the comments is one nobody has cooked.

fixes.title: Get the AI notetaker out of your meeting
fixes.summary: Remove the bot that joined uninvited, and stop yours from joining others.
fixes.changes: No transcript or summary is generated, and the silent participant leaves.
steps: In the meeting: open Participants, find the entry with "Notetaker", "AI Companion", "Otter" or similar, and remove it as you would any participant. Hosts can do this; you may need to ask the host.
Zoom: Settings → AI Companion → turn off meeting summary and smart recording. Account owners control it at zoom.us/profile/setting.
Google Meet: the host controls "Take notes for me"; ask them to turn it off. Recording and transcription are separate switches.
Teams: remove Copilot and any notetaker app from the meeting; your administrator controls whether it can be added at all.
Say at the start that you object. In most jurisdictions recording a meeting requires notice, and in several it requires consent.
caveats: In a workplace, the administrator's policy may override your personal setting.
Third-party notetakers join as ordinary participants, so removing them works exactly like removing a person.
Consent law varies. Objecting out loud is both polite and, in some places, legally significant.

fixes.title: News without a generated briefing on top
fixes.summary: Skip the aggregator's summary and go to the publications, or to a human-edited front page.
fixes.changes: You read headlines written by editors rather than a digest assembled by a model.

alternatives.label: Ground News — see the same story across outlets

fixes.how: Wire services and public broadcasters still run human-edited front pages. Ground News shows you how differently the same event is being reported, which no summary can do.
caveats: Google News offers no way to remove its generated briefings.
Ground News has a free tier; its most useful comparison features are paid.

fixes.title: Read the news in the order it was published
fixes.summary: Subscribe to publications directly. No feed algorithm, no summary, no suggestions.
fixes.changes: You see every article from the sources you chose, newest first, and nothing else.
fixes.how: RSS is a plain list of a site's newest articles that almost every publication still produces, usually without advertising it. A reader collects them into one chronological list.
steps: Pick a reader. NetNewsWire is free with no account and syncs via iCloud.
Add sites by pasting their address; the reader usually finds the feed itself.
Most newspapers, blogs, YouTube channels and even some Reddit forums have feeds.
Check it once or twice a day rather than continuously; that is the real benefit.
caveats: Some publications provide headline-only feeds to drive clicks.
Feedly has added AI features; NetNewsWire and Miniflux have none at all.

fixes.title: Strip a page down to its words
fixes.summary: Reader mode removes advertisements, pop-ups, related-article machinery and most inserted widgets.
fixes.changes: The article appears as plain text on a plain background, in a typeface you choose.
steps: iPhone Safari: tap the page-settings icon at the left of the address bar, then "Show Reader". Hold it to set a site to always open this way.
Firefox: the page icon in the address bar, or Ctrl+Alt+R.
Chrome desktop: enable Reading Mode from the three-dot menu → More tools.
Android Chrome: it offers "Simplified view" automatically on long articles; enable it in Settings → Accessibility.
fixes.how: Reader mode reconstructs the page from its article text alone. Anything injected around the article — including most generated summaries and suggestion panels — is simply not carried over.
caveats: It fails on pages with unusual layouts, and on some paywalled articles.
Safari's "always use Reader" per-site setting is the most useful part and the least known.

fixes.title: Translate without the commentary
fixes.summary: Get the translation itself, without an assistant offering to explain, rewrite or expand it.
fixes.changes: Text in, text out. The web version is quieter than the apps.

alternatives.label: Wiktionary, for a single word done properly

fixes.how: Machine translation has always been statistical; the objection is usually to the assistant layered on top of it. DeepL's translator page is still just two boxes, and Wiktionary gives you etymology, usage and register that no translator will.
caveats: All machine translation is a machine. If you want a human, a professional translator is the answer and there is no substitute for one in legal or medical matters.
Both services process your text on their servers. Do not paste anything confidential.

fixes.title: A weather forecast, plainly stated
fixes.summary: Go to the meteorological office rather than an app that narrates the forecast at you.
fixes.changes: You get the official forecast, the charts, and the warnings, written by meteorologists.
fixes.how: Most consumer weather apps resell the same national model data with a layer of interpretation on top. Going to the source removes the layer and is usually more accurate for warnings.
caveats: Official sites are less pretty and occasionally slower on a phone. Add one to your home screen and it behaves like an app.
Yr, run by the Norwegian broadcaster and meteorological institute, covers the whole world and is free of advertising.

fixes.title: Keep generated edits out of your photographs
fixes.service: Google Photos, Apple Photos, Samsung Gallery
fixes.summary: Turn off the automatic enhancements and know where the edit labels live.
fixes.changes: Your photographs stay as taken, and edited ones carry a visible note that they were altered.
steps: iPhone: turning off Apple Intelligence removes Clean Up from the Photos editor. Settings → Apple Intelligence & Siri.
Google Photos: the Magic Editor and Best Take are opt-in per edit; edited images carry an "AI info" note in their details.
Samsung: Settings → Advanced features → Galaxy AI, and in Gallery turn off automatic suggestions. Samsung stamps generated edits with a watermark and metadata.
To check any photograph: open its information panel and look for an AI or edit note.
caveats: Computational photography — the processing every phone does when the shutter is pressed — cannot be turned off, and is not what this entry is about. Shooting in RAW comes closest.
Edit labels survive in the file's metadata but are lost if the image is screenshotted.

fixes.title: Learn from a person, not a summary
fixes.summary: Where to go when you want the subject explained by somebody who knows it.
fixes.changes: You get depth, disagreement and somebody to ask, instead of a confident paragraph.

action.label: Find it in a library
action.placeholder: A subject you want to understand

fixes.how: A public library card gives you free access to books, and usually to paid course platforms and newspaper archives as well. It remains the best-value institution in the world.
caveats: Library digital lending varies enormously by country and council.

fixes.title: Maps without the generated recommendations
fixes.summary: Turn off the personalised suggestions, or use a map that never had any.
fixes.changes: You get a map and directions. Nothing suggests restaurants or summarises reviews at you.
fixes.how: OpenStreetMap is built by volunteers surveying places themselves. Organic Maps uses that data in a phone app that works offline and has no advertising, accounts or recommendation engine.
caveats: Business opening hours and live traffic are much weaker than Google's.
Organic Maps is excellent for walking, cycling and travel abroad; less so for city driving.

fixes.title: See a page as it was before
fixes.summary: Read the version of an article or recipe from before the site was rewritten.
fixes.changes: You get the original text, often shorter and better, without the additions made since.
fixes.how: The Internet Archive has been keeping copies of the web since 1996. Paste any address and choose a date before the change you dislike.
steps: Copy the address of the page.
Paste it into web.archive.org.
Pick a year from the calendar — 2018 to 2021 is usually a good span for recipes and how-to writing.
caveats: Not every page is archived, and interactive pages often do not work.
The archive is a charity. If you use it often, consider donating.
